subtopics.title: What a Percentage Really Is — and the Decimal Trick

questions.question: 15% of R800 is:
The single multiplier for a 15% DECREASE is:
The single multiplier for a 15% INCREASE is:
Why is the multiplier method preferred over 'find the percentage, then add or subtract'?
options: It compresses the whole change into one multiplication and handles chained changes cleanly
It always gives a rounder answer
It is the only accepted method

subtopics.title: The Discount Step, Then the VAT Step

questions.question: After the 15% discount, the sneakers cost:
The VAT step must be applied to:
options: The discounted price of R680 — each step works on the previous result

questions.question: The final price of the sneakers, after discount then VAT, is:
Why do the −15% and +15% NOT cancel out?
options: They do cancel — the final price is R800
Because the discount was applied second
The VAT acted on the smaller discounted price, so it put back R102 where the discount removed R120
Because VAT is calculated only on luxury goods

subtopics.title: The Single Percentage Change — One Multiplier for the Whole Journey

questions.question: The combined multiplier for the whole journey (×0,85 then ×1,15) is:
A combined multiplier of 0,9775 means the overall change is:
In the percentage change formula, the denominator is always:
options: The original value — the reference point where you started
The larger of the two values

subtopics.title: Reverse Percentages — and the Full Toolkit

questions.question: A price of R782 INCLUDES 15% VAT. The price before VAT is found by:
Why is 'subtract 15%' (×0,85) WRONG for removing VAT from a VAT-inclusive price?
options: It is correct — both methods agree
The VAT was calculated on the before-VAT price, so 15% of the final price is the wrong amount to remove

questions.question: To undo any percentage multiplier, you:
options: Multiply by the same multiplier again

questions.question: R782 ÷ 1,15 returns exactly R680. What does this confirm?
options: The reverse calculation recovers the discounted pre-VAT price — the whole chain is consistent

questions.question: A shop takes 15% off a price. What percentage of the price is still on the slab?
R800 × 0,85 = R680. What does the 0,85 stand for?
options: The 85% that remains after 15% comes off
The number of items in the sale

questions.question: A R150 airtime voucher carries a 20% bonus. The one-step calculation is:

subtopics.title: Two Fifteens That Refuse to Cancel

questions.question: 15% of R800 is R120. How much is 15% of R680?
Why do the sneakers end at R782 instead of back at R800?
options: The VAT was worked out on the smaller R680, so it put back R18 less than the discount removed
The shop rounded the cents away
VAT in South Africa is only 10%

questions.question: 0,85 × 1,15 = 0,9775. In plain words, the final price is:
The sneakers dropped R18 in total. To turn that into a percentage you divide it by:
options: R800, the price you started at

questions.question: A till slip reads R782 including 15% VAT. To find the price before VAT you:
Taking 15% off R782 gives R664,70. Why is that the wrong pre-VAT price?
options: It removes 15% of the bigger final price — R117,30 — which is more VAT than the R102 ever charged
The multiplication itself was done wrong

questions.question: The VAT got onto the price by multiplying. It comes off again by:
options: Multiplying by the same number again

questions.question: R680 + R102 = R782. What are those two amounts?
options: The original price and the discount
The final price and the change owed
The price before VAT and the VAT charged on it
